note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Perform advanced welding using manual metal arc welding process (MMAW)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A job's WPS (welding procedure specification) covers positions 1G, 2G and 3G only. One pipe joint on the job must be welded in the 5G position. What should the team leader do?
options: Weld it on the same WPS, since 5G is close to the 3G position
Get a WPS that covers 5G, and a welder qualified for it
Lower the current by about 10% and weld it on the same WPS
Give it to the welder with the most years in the trade

questions.stem: Why does a supervisor check the welders' qualification records before giving out the welds on a pressure pipe job?
options: To confirm each is tested for that process, position and material
To find the welder on the team who charges the lowest hourly rate
To see which welder has signed out the fewest electrodes this month
Because the records show which welder can finish the job the fastest

questions.stem: A drawing calls for a 'full penetration' butt weld on a beam splice. What does this mean for the welder?
options: The cap must stand at least 5 mm above the plate surface
The joint may be welded from one side with no root gap
The weld must fuse through the whole thickness of the joint
The weld must be ground flush on both faces when done

questions.stem: The mill certificate for a thick structural plate shows a high carbon equivalent (CE). What does this tell the supervisor?
options: The steel is easier to weld and needs no special care
The steel is more likely to crack, so preheat may be needed
The steel may only be welded with E6013 electrodes
The steel can be welded at a higher travel speed than usual

questions.stem: A welder must weld inside a large steel tank at a factory in Spanish Town. Which arrangement is correct?
options: Permit, gas test, forced air and a standby person outside
A hose inside the tank blowing pure oxygen to freshen the air
Work alone inside with the hatch shut to keep the fumes in
Open the hatch and start, as a large tank holds plenty of air

questions.stem: Why does overhead MMAW need more protection for the head and shoulders than flat welding?
options: The arc is brighter when the electrode points upward
Less fume is made overhead, so the hood is pushed back
The electrode carries more current in the overhead position
Hot spatter and slag fall down onto the welder

questions.stem: On a site in Ocho Rios, a weld is 4 m up on a steel frame. What must be in place before welding starts?
options: A ladder held by a trainee, with the welding cable tied to the ladder
Only a hard hat, as long as the welder takes great care
A safe work platform or fall protection, and a fire watch below
A rope from the welder's belt to the welding machine below

questions.stem: MMAW of stainless steel gives off fume containing hexavalent chromium. Which control should come first?
options: A fan behind the welder blowing the fume across the shop
Extraction at the arc, with a respirator if still needed
A thin paper dust mask, with the workshop door shut
Welding faster so that the job makes less fume

questions.stem: Why should a welder never wrap the electrode cable around their body or shoulders while welding?
options: A damaged cable could shock them, and it adds magnetic field exposure
The cable gets far too hot to use when it is wrapped round in tight coils
Wrapping the cable cuts the welding current to half its setting
The cable wears out faster when it rubs on the welding jacket

questions.stem: An engine-driven welder is used on a building site. Where should it be placed?
options: Inside the building beside the job, to keep the welding cables short
In a closed container to keep the rain off it
Under the stairwell, where it is out of everyone's way
Outdoors, away from doors and windows, so exhaust cannot build up

questions.stem: A 6G pipe test uses an E6010 root and E7018 fill and cap. Why is a machine with DC output chosen?
options: AC cannot strike and hold an arc on a curved pipe surface in position
DC uses less electricity than AC in every case
E6010 runs on DC only, and DC gives a steadier arc out of position
DC stops arc blow from happening on pipe

questions.stem: What does the arc force (dig) control on an MMAW inverter do?
options: It sets the open-circuit voltage of the machine's voltage reduction device
It raises the current when the arc gets short, so the rod does not stick
It switches the polarity from electrode positive to electrode negative
It sets how long the machine can run before it must rest

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of a remote current control when welding a large pipe in position?
options: The welder can change the current at the joint without leaving it
It means the welding current never needs to be checked with a meter
It lets the machine run past its rated duty cycle safely
It changes the electrode type to suit each position

questions.stem: Which electrode is normally used for the root run of a cross-country pipeline welded vertical-down?
options: A rutile electrode such as E6013
An iron powder electrode such as E7024
A hardfacing electrode
A cellulosic electrode such as E6010

questions.stem: Why is an E7024 (high iron powder) electrode not used for vertical or overhead welds?
options: It will only run on DC electrode negative
It deposits far too little weld metal for those joints
Its large, fluid pool cannot be held against gravity
Its flux is too thin to form any slag

questions.stem: A packet of E7018 electrodes was left open on a bench overnight in a humid workshop. What should the supervisor do?
options: Use them, since the flux dries out in the heat of the arc
Have them re-dried as the maker says, or scrap them
Use them only for the root run, where it does not matter
Warm each one on the hot job for a minute before use

questions.stem: Which electrode is normally used to weld grade 304 stainless steel to itself?
options: E7018 low-hydrogen
E308L stainless
E6013 rutile
E6010 cellulosic

questions.stem: A mild steel bracket must be welded to a stainless steel tank with MMAW. Which electrode is usually chosen?
options: E309L, made for joining unlike steels
E308L, the same as for stainless to stainless
E6013, because the bracket is mild steel
E7018, because it is a low-hydrogen type

questions.stem: Why is a nickel-based electrode often used to repair cast iron by MMAW?
options: Nickel needs no cleaning or grinding of the casting before welding
Nickel makes the cast iron much harder than before
Nickel runs at a much higher current than steel rods
Nickel weld metal stays soft and ductile, so it resists cracking

questions.stem: What is hardfacing?
options: Grinding a weld cap flush and polishing it smooth
Welding with the electrode held hard against the work
Laying a wear-resistant deposit on a part, such as a bucket tooth
Heating a hard weld until it glows red, so that it becomes soft again

questions.stem: A single-V butt joint in 12 mm plate is to be welded from one side with full penetration. Which fit-up is a WPS most likely to give?
options: About 60° included angle, 2–3 mm root gap, 1–2 mm root face
About 30° included angle, no gap, 6 mm root face
About 90° included angle, 6 mm gap, no root face
About 45° included angle, no gap, 4 mm root face

questions.stem: Why is a double-V preparation often chosen for plate 20 mm thick or more?
options: It means the joint never needs back gouging from the other side
It needs less weld metal and helps balance distortion
It can be welded completely from one side only
It needs no root face and no root gap at all

questions.stem: Why are the ends of each tack weld on a pipe root ground to a feather edge?
options: So the root run fuses into the tack with no lump or lack of fusion
So the tacks can be seen more easily by the inspector at the end of the job
So the tacks can be knocked off later with a hammer
So the root run can be made at a lower current

questions.stem: A WPS calls for 100 °C preheat on 25 mm plate. How should the preheat be checked?
options: Touch the plate with a gloved hand to feel the heat
With a temperature crayon or thermometer, back from the joint edge
By the colour of the steel, which glows dull red at 100 °C
By timing the heating torch at one minute for each 10 mm of thickness

questions.stem: How does preheat help to stop hydrogen cracking in thick steel?
options: It burns the hydrogen out of the electrode coating
It makes the arc longer and smoother
It slows cooling, so hydrogen escapes and hard zones are less likely
It removes the mill scale so no grinding is needed

questions.stem: What is meant by the interpass temperature?
options: The temperature inside the electrode oven
The temperature of the weld pool itself while welding is going on
The air temperature in the workshop that day
The temperature of the joint just before the next run

questions.stem: When welding vertical-up on 10 mm plate with E7018, how is the electrode usually held?
options: Almost square to the plate, tilted slightly upward
Pointing down the joint at about 45°
Laid almost flat along the joint, pointing up
Pointing down at 45°, dragging the slag behind

questions.stem: Why is vertical-down welding with E7018 usually not allowed on structural work?
options: Downhill welding is slower and wastes more electrodes
Downhill welding gives far too much penetration and burns through the root
With most low-hydrogen rods it gives lack of fusion and slag traps
Downhill welding needs AC, which E7018 cannot run on

questions.stem: When welding overhead (4G), what is the main way to stop the pool from dripping?
options: Use a long arc so the pool cools before it can fall
Keep a short arc and a small pool, using stringer beads
Use the largest electrode so the pool is held up
Turn the current up so the metal freezes faster

questions.stem: On a horizontal butt weld (2G), how are the fill and cap runs usually laid?
options: As one wide weave from the bottom edge to the top edge
From the top plate downward, letting each run sag onto the last
As one heavy run made with the largest electrode
As stringer beads from the bottom up, each overlapping the last

questions.stem: Why is the 6G pipe position seen as the hardest test position?
options: The welder meets flat, vertical and overhead angles on a sloping joint
The pipe is turned during welding, so the welder must work hard to keep up
Only AC current can be used when the pipe is set at 45°
The whole joint must be welded with a single electrode

questions.stem: What is the hot pass in a pipe weld?
options: The final cap run, laid at the highest current
A tack weld made before the root run
The run straight after the root, to fuse it and burn out slag lines
A run made only to preheat the pipe

questions.stem: On a 5G pipe root, the bottom (overhead) part shows a hollow root on the inside, called suck-back. Which change usually helps?
options: Use a longer arc at the bottom of the pipe so the pool can spread out
Keep a tight arc and push the electrode further into the joint
Travel faster through the bottom section
Open the root gap to about 6 mm

questions.stem: A long fillet weld on a beam is made in short lengths, each started ahead and welded back towards the last one. What is this called?
options: Back-step welding
Weave welding
Stringer welding
Tack welding

questions.stem: Two plates are set at a small angle before a single-V butt weld is made. Why?
options: To make room for a backing bar under the joint
To keep the root gap from opening during welding
So that the slag runs away from the joint
So that weld shrinkage pulls them flat

questions.stem: Why is a balanced welding sequence used on a large built-up beam?
options: So that two welders can share one machine
To use fewer electrodes on the whole job
So shrinkage on one side is balanced by the other
So the beam can be welded without any tacks

questions.stem: A radiograph shows a long dark line along the side of a multi-run butt weld. What is it most likely to be?
options: Lack of side-wall fusion or a slag line
Too much reinforcement on the cap
Spatter stuck to the cap surface
A change in the plate's thickness

questions.stem: A large bead of excess metal hangs below the root of a plate butt weld. Which is a likely cause?
options: Root gap too small and current too low
Root gap too wide or current too high for the root
Electrodes stored in a heated oven
Plate cleaned too well before tacking

questions.stem: A crack is found in a butt weld on a structural job. How should the repair start?
options: Weld a cap run over the crack to seal it, then grind it flush to match
Fill it with body filler and paint over it
Peen it with a hammer until it closes
Grind it out fully, check it is gone, then follow a repair procedure

questions.stem: Which test is quick and cheap for finding surface cracks in a stainless steel weld, which is not magnetic?
options: Magnetic particle testing
Hardness testing
Dye penetrant testing
Nick-break testing

questions.stem: A WPS says the cap of a butt weld must not stand more than 3 mm above the plate. A cap measures 4.5 mm. What should happen?
options: Record it as not conforming, dress it to the limit and check again
Accept it, because extra weld metal on the cap makes the joint stronger
Add another cap run on top to even out the shape
Cut out the whole weld and start the joint again

questions.stem: Which tool is used to measure the cap height and undercut depth on a butt weld?
options: A spirit level
A bridge cam weld gauge
A centre square
A pair of dividers

questions.stem: In a welder test on 6G pipe, bend strips are cut from more than one place around the pipe. Why?
options: So that the rest of the pipe can be used again
Because one strip is always too short to bend
To use up the whole test pipe so that none of the expensive pipe is wasted
So each strip tests a different position, such as vertical and overhead

questions.stem: You supervise two welders on a site job. One is welding a joint to a WPS he has not read. What is the best action?
options: Let him finish this joint, then ask him to read the WPS before the next one
Swap him with a trainee who has read the WPS
Stop him, go through the WPS together, and check the welds done so far
Write him up and let him carry on welding

questions.stem: Why is each welder's ID number recorded against each weld on a structural job?
options: So each welder is paid by the number of welds
So each weld can be traced to the welder who made it
So the steel supplier can be contacted about it
So the painters know which weld to paint first

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the process of lightly hammering a hot weld run, often on cast iron repairs, to relieve shrinkage stress?
In the trade, what one-word name is often used for a welder's qualification certificate?
What do the letters CE stand for, as a figure worked out from a steel's chemistry to judge its risk of cracking?
A pipe has an outside diameter of 168 mm. About how long is the weld round it, in mm, to the nearest 10 mm? (Use π = 3.14.)
What do the letters VRD stand for on an MMAW machine?
What is the name for a weld run laid in a straight line with little or no side-to-side movement?
What do the letters NDT stand for?
What is the name for cutting the back of the first side of a double-V weld down to sound metal before welding the second side?
A vertical-up root is welded at 120 A. The WPS says the fill runs use 15% more current. What current, in amps, should be set for the fill?
On a weld symbol, which shape is drawn where the arrow meets the reference line to show 'weld all round'?
When a fixed horizontal pipe is described like a clock face, which time marks the very bottom of the pipe?
A WPS calls for a minimum preheat of 75 °C. The plate measures 58 °C. By how many degrees Celsius must it be raised before welding?
What is the name of the fault where weld metal flows onto the plate beyond the toe without fusing to it?
What is the name of the distance from the root of a fillet weld to the middle of its face, which sets the weld's strength?
Which gas, picked up from damp flux, rust or grease, causes cold cracking in hard steels?

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare, tack and weld a carbon steel pipe butt joint in the 5G position with MMAW, from the root to the cap. Include the electrodes and the direction of travel.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the WPS for the pipe size, bevel, root gap, electrodes and current. The pipe ends are bevelled to about 30° each side (a 60° included angle), with a small root face, and cleaned to bright metal inside and out. I set the root gap with a spacer and put three or four small tacks round the pipe, grinding their ends to a feather edge. The pipe is fixed with its axis level. The root is run uphill with an E6010 or the root electrode the WPS gives, starting just past the 6 o'clock position and going up each side to 12 o'clock, keeping a small keyhole. I clean and grind the root, lay a hot pass, then fill and cap with E7018 uphill, cleaning every run and staggering the stops and starts. Finally I check the profile and record the welder and settings.
markingPoints: Checks the WPS, then bevels and cleans the pipe ends with the correct root face and gap
Tacks evenly with feathered ends and fixes the pipe with its axis level
Root run uphill from the bottom to the top on each side, keeping a keyhole
Cleans between runs; hot pass, then fill and cap with low-hydrogen electrodes
Staggers stops and starts, checks the finished weld and records it

essays.stem: Compare vertical-up and overhead MMAW of a single-V butt joint in 10 mm plate. Cover the current, electrode angle, bead pattern and the defects to watch for in each.
essays.modelAnswer: In both positions the current is set a little lower than for flat welding, so the pool stays small and can be controlled. For vertical-up the electrode is held almost square to the plate and tilted slightly upward. The fill and cap are often laid with a side-to-side or triangle weave, pausing at each edge so the sides fuse and undercut is avoided. The main defects are undercut at the edges, a peaked or sagging cap and slag trapped at the sides. For overhead the electrode is held almost square with a slight drag angle, the arc is kept very short, and stringer beads are used instead of a wide weave. The main risks are the pool dripping, a convex bead with slag trapped at the toes, and lack of fusion if the welder rushes.
markingPoints: Lower current than flat in both positions, to keep a small pool
Vertical-up: electrode near square, tilted up, weave with a pause at the edges
Overhead: short arc, small stringer beads, not a wide weave
Vertical defects: undercut, sagging cap, slag at the sides
Overhead defects: dripping, convex bead, slag at the toes, lack of fusion

essays.stem: Explain how a supervisor decides whether a thick steel joint needs preheat, and describe how preheat and interpass temperature are applied, measured and recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: The supervisor first reads the WPS and the drawing. The need for preheat depends on the steel's carbon equivalent from the mill certificate, the joint thickness, how tightly the joint is held (restraint), the hydrogen level of the electrode and the weather. Thicker, harder steel and damp conditions all raise the risk of hydrogen cracking, so the WPS sets a minimum preheat. Heat is applied evenly with a gas heating torch or electric heating pads, all round the joint and some distance either side. The temperature is checked with a temperature crayon or contact thermometer on the plate a short way back from the joint edge, before welding and between runs. If the joint gets hotter than the maximum interpass temperature, welding stops until it cools. The readings, times and welder are written on the weld record.
markingPoints: Uses the WPS: carbon equivalent, thickness, restraint, electrode hydrogen level
Explains that preheat slows cooling and lowers the risk of hydrogen cracking
Heats evenly round the joint with a heating torch or heating pads
Measures with a crayon or thermometer back from the joint edge, before and between runs
Keeps within the maximum interpass temperature and records the readings

essays.stem: Explain how you would weld a mild steel bracket to a stainless steel tank by MMAW. Include the electrode choice, cleaning, heat control and how you would stop the stainless steel being spoiled.
essays.modelAnswer: Joining unlike steels needs an electrode made for the job, usually E309L, so the weld metal stays tough and does not crack when it mixes with the mild steel. I would check the WPS or ask the supervisor to confirm this. Both parts are cleaned of oil, paint and scale. The stainless is cleaned only with a stainless steel brush and grinding discs kept for stainless, so that iron particles do not get into it and cause rust spots. I would use the lowest current that gives good fusion, small stringer runs, and let the job cool between runs, because too much heat warps the thin tank and harms its resistance to corrosion. Extraction is used because stainless fume contains chromium. After welding, the slag is removed and the heat tint cleaned by the method the Centre allows.
markingPoints: Chooses an electrode made for unlike steels, such as E309L, as the WPS says
Cleans both parts; uses stainless-only brushes and discs on the stainless
Low current, stringer runs and cooling between runs to limit heat
Uses extraction because of chromium in the fume
Cleans the slag and the heat tint after welding

essays.stem: Describe how to repair a cracked cast iron pump body by MMAW so that the repair does not crack again.
essays.modelAnswer: I first clean the casting of oil and dirt, then find both ends of the crack, using dye penetrant if needed. A small hole is drilled at each end to stop the crack running. The crack is ground out into a U or V groove down to sound metal. The casting is warmed gently and evenly, as the procedure says, to reduce the stress from welding. I weld with a nickel-based electrode, which gives a soft, ductile deposit. The runs are short, about 25 to 40 mm, and made at low current. Each run is peened lightly with a round-nosed hammer while it is still hot, to relieve shrinkage stress. I wait for the area to cool before the next short run and spread the runs along the crack. Finally the casting is cooled slowly, covered or wrapped, and checked again for cracks.
markingPoints: Cleans and finds the ends of the crack; drills a stop hole at each end
Grinds out the crack to sound metal
Gentle, even preheat as the procedure says; nickel-based electrode
Short runs at low current, peened while hot, with cooling between runs
Slow cooling and a final check for cracks

essays.stem: A long I-beam is to be built up from three plates with continuous fillet welds. Explain how you would plan the tacking, welding sequence and checks to keep it straight.
essays.modelAnswer: Before welding I check the plates are straight and the web is square to the flanges, and clamp the parts in a jig or on a flat table. I tack at even spaces along both sides of the web, putting tacks opposite each other so the pull is balanced. The four fillet welds are planned so that shrinkage on one side is balanced by shrinkage on the other. Where possible, two welders weld opposite sides at the same time, working from the middle towards the ends. If only one welder is used, the runs are made in a set order on opposite fillets, using back-step or skip lengths and letting the beam cool between runs. I check the beam with a string line and square during the work, and change the order if it starts to bow. At the end I measure the straightness and record it.
markingPoints: Checks parts and fit-up; clamps in a jig or on a flat table
Tacks at even spaces, opposite each other
Plans a balanced sequence on opposite fillets, from the middle outward
Uses back-step or skip welding with cooling time
Checks straightness during and after welding, adjusts the sequence and records it

essays.stem: Explain how a welder qualification test on 6G pipe is set up, carried out and tested, and what the welder's certificate allows them to weld afterwards.
essays.modelAnswer: The test follows a written procedure that gives the pipe size and wall thickness, the bevel and gap, the electrodes and the current range. The test coupon is marked with the welder's number and fixed with its axis at 45° so it cannot be moved. The inspector checks the fit-up and watches the welding. The welder makes the root, hot pass, fill and cap, stopping and starting as normal, but must not turn the pipe or grind away faults unless the rules allow it. The finished weld is inspected by eye for its profile, undercut and root penetration. Strips are then cut from set places round the pipe and bent, or the weld is X-rayed. If it passes, the certificate lists the process, the electrode group, the thickness and diameter range and the positions the welder is qualified for. It must be kept up to date.
markingPoints: Test to a written procedure: pipe size, bevel, electrodes, current
Coupon marked and fixed at 45°; the inspector checks fit-up and watches
Visual inspection, then bend strips from set places or radiography
The certificate lists the process, electrode, thickness, diameter and positions covered
The qualification must be kept current and is checked before jobs are given

essays.stem: Explain the hazards of MMAW inside a steel tank, and describe the permit and controls you, as team leader, would put in place.
essays.modelAnswer: A tank is a confined space. The air inside may be short of oxygen or may hold flammable or toxic gas from what the tank held. Welding fume and heat build up fast, the steel walls make electric shock more likely, and getting a hurt person out is hard. Before work, I would get a confined space entry permit and a hot work permit. The tank is emptied, cleaned and isolated from all pipes, and the air is tested by a trained person before entry and during the work. Forced ventilation or extraction is set up, never oxygen. The welder uses a machine with a voltage reduction device, dry gloves and an insulating mat. A trained standby person stays outside the whole time, with a way to talk to the welder and a rescue plan and equipment ready. Gas cylinders stay outside the tank.
markingPoints: Names hazards: low oxygen, toxic or flammable gas, fume, heat, shock, rescue
Confined space and hot work permits; tank emptied, cleaned and isolated
Air tested before and during the work; forced ventilation, never oxygen
Shock controls: voltage reduction device, dry PPE, insulating mat
Standby person outside, communication and a rescue plan; cylinders kept out

essays.stem: Describe how a double-V butt joint in 25 mm plate is welded with MMAW, including back gouging, and explain why the runs are balanced between the two sides.
essays.modelAnswer: The plate edges are bevelled on both sides to the angles in the WPS, with a small root face and gap, and cleaned. The joint is tacked and, if needed, preheated to the WPS figure. I weld the root and two or three runs on the first side. The plate is then turned over and the back of the root is gouged out, with air carbon arc gouging or a grinder, until sound, clean metal shows. The gouged groove is ground smooth and checked, often with dye penetrant or magnetic particles, before the second side is welded. After that I weld a few runs on each side in turn rather than finishing one side first. Weld metal shrinks as it cools, so balancing the runs makes the shrinkage on each side pull against the other, which keeps the plate flat. Each run is cleaned and the interpass temperature checked.
markingPoints: Bevels both sides with root face and gap; cleans, tacks and preheats as the WPS says
Welds the root and first runs on side one
Back-gouges to sound metal, grinds smooth and checks before welding side two
Alternates runs between the sides to balance shrinkage and limit distortion
Cleans each run and checks the interpass temperature

essays.stem: As team leader on a structural job, describe the weld records you would keep, and how you would use visual inspection results to coach the welders in your team.
essays.modelAnswer: For each weld I would keep a record linked to a weld map: the weld number, the WPS used, the welder's ID, the electrode batch, any preheat readings, the date, and the visual inspection result with any NDT results. Repairs are recorded too, with the reason. I would also keep the welders' qualification records and the electrode oven log. Each week I would look through the visual inspection results for patterns, such as one welder having undercut on vertical welds, or many stop-start faults. I would then watch that welder at work, show the right technique, for example a shorter arc and a pause at the edges, and let them practise on scrap. I would praise the improvement and check their next welds. If a fault appears across the whole team, I would hold a short toolbox talk on it.
markingPoints: Weld record linked to a weld map: weld number, WPS, welder, electrode batch, preheat, date
Records inspection results, NDT and repairs
Keeps qualification records and the electrode oven log
Looks for patterns in the results by welder or by fault
Coaches by watching, showing the right technique, practice and re-checking; talks to the team if needed

practical1.title: Planned vertical-up (3G) and overhead (4G) butt welds on 10 mm plate, with inspection and bend tests
practical1.brief: As a group, read the welding procedure the assessor gives you and write a short weld plan: who welds which test piece, the electrodes, the current range, the fit-up and the order of work. Each member then prepares, tacks and welds one single-V butt joint in 10 mm carbon steel plate in the vertical-up position (3G) and a second one in the overhead position (4G), using E7018 electrodes (or those the procedure gives). Members take turns as welder and as inspector: the inspector checks the fit-up and records the current used. When the welds are cool, the group inspects every weld by eye and with a weld gauge and fills in a weld record. The assessor cuts and bends one strip from each weld, and the group records the results. Photograph each stage below and add the photos and the completed weld plan and record to the group's practical.
materials: Pairs of 10 mm carbon steel plate, about 150 mm × 100 mm, bevelled for a single-V (two pairs per member)
E7018 electrodes (3.2 mm and 2.5 mm) from a heated oven, or those the procedure gives
DC welding machines and positioners or stands for vertical and overhead work
Weld gauges, a steel rule and a temperature crayon
Grinder, chipping hammer and wire brush
The welding procedure, a weld plan sheet and a weld record sheet
photos: A member's test piece tacked, with the gap and root face measured
A test piece fixed in the vertical-up position, with the welder in full PPE
A test piece fixed overhead, with the welder in full PPE
The finished 3G and 4G weld faces and roots for each member
A weld gauge on a cap, measuring its height
The bent strips, labelled with each member's number
The completed weld record and the cleaned work area
checklist: Helped write the weld plan and followed it
Wore full PPE, including head and shoulder cover for overhead welding
Prepared and tacked the joint to the procedure's gap and root face
Set the current within the procedure's range and recorded it
Controlled the pool in both positions: correct electrode angle, arc length and bead pattern
Cleaned each run fully before the next
Inspected welds with a gauge and recorded results accurately
Bend strips showed no opening or cracks beyond what the procedure allows
Left the area safe, with stubs in a metal container and electrodes back in the oven
safety: Weld only in booths or behind screens; warn others before striking an arc
Wear a cap or hood, a buttoned collar and leather sleeves when welding overhead
Keep gloves and clothing dry; check cables and holders before use
Use extraction or good ventilation and keep your head out of the fume
Treat test pieces as hot; use tongs and mark them HOT
Only the assessor operates the bending machine; stand clear while strips are bent

practical2.title: Fixed 5G pipe butt weld with a cellulosic root and low-hydrogen fill and cap, with a weld record
practical2.brief: Each member welds one carbon steel pipe butt joint, about 100 mm to 150 mm outside diameter with a wall of about 6 mm to 8 mm (the size the Centre has), fixed with its axis horizontal (5G). The group first plans the job together: the bevel and gap, the tack positions, the electrodes for the root (E6010 or as the procedure gives), the hot pass, and the E7018 fill and cap, and the current for each. Each member bevels or checks the pipe ends, sets the gap and tacks, and welds the root uphill from the bottom to the top on each side. They clean and grind the root, then weld the hot pass, fill and cap. While one member welds, another acts as inspector, checking the fit-up and recording the settings on the weld record. The group then inspects every pipe weld inside and out and records the results. Photograph each stage and add the photos and the weld record to the group's practical.
materials: Carbon steel pipe sections, about 100 mm long, with bevelled ends (two per member)
E6010 (or the procedure's root electrode) and E7018 electrodes, the E7018 from a heated oven
DC welding machines and pipe stands that fix the pipe in the 5G position
Grinder with thin discs, chipping hammer, wire brush and files
Weld gauge, inspection mirror and torch
The welding procedure and a weld record sheet
photos: The group's written plan for the pipe weld
A pipe pair tacked, showing the gap and feathered tacks
The pipe fixed in the 5G stand

checklist: Took part in the plan and named the right electrode for each run
Prepared and tacked the pipe with an even gap and feathered tacks
Welded the root uphill from the bottom, with even penetration on the inside
Ground and cleaned the root and each later run
Changed electrode angle and arc length correctly round the pipe
Finished cap even, with no undercut, porosity or cracks
Recorded settings and inspection results accurately as inspector
Worked safely and left the area clean
safety: Check the machine, cables and holder before use; keep gloves dry
Wear full PPE, with head cover when welding the bottom of the pipe
Use extraction or good ventilation; cellulosic rods make a lot of fume
Keep flammable material away and an extinguisher at hand
Treat pipes as hot after welding; use tongs and mark them HOT
